title: Paul McCartney asks Tony Visconti to orchestrate Band On The Run | 1973
content:
On 13 October 1973, Paul McCartney telephoned producer and arranger Tony Visconti to enquire about him orchestrating seven songs on the Band On The Run album.

The songs were ‘Band On The Run’, ‘Jet’, ‘Bluebird’, ‘Mrs Vandebilt’, ‘No Words’, ‘Picasso’s Last Words (Drink To Me)’, and ‘Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five’.

Visconti had produced hit records for David Bowie and T.Rex, and was married to McCartney’s former protégé Mary Hopkin.

In search of a new direction, and possibly to give an injection of something different, Paul and Linda, along with Denny Laine, had gone to Lagos in Nigeria to make their next album. In late September [sic], shortly after they returned we got a phone call at our home from Macca. After he talked briefly to Mary she handed me the phone.

‘Hi Tony, I love the strings on T.Rex records, did you write them?’
‘Yes,’ I replied.
‘Can you really read and write music?’
‘Yes.’
‘Oh right, in that case will you write strings for the album I’ve just finished?’
‘YES!’

Tony Visconti
Bowie, Bolan And The Brooklyn Boy

They met the following day at McCartney’s London home to discuss the arrangements. The overdub session took place on 17 October 1973.
